title: kind-'test' now runs every matching test in the directory, not just the requested target

finding.claim: kind-'test' now runs every matching test in the directory, not just the requested target
finding.evidence: The new unittest invocation discovers tests from the target directory using the target basename as a pattern, so a request for one file can execute additional matching files and fail or pass based on unrelated tests in that directory.
finding.recommendation: Limit execution to the requested test module or file instead of directory-wide discovery. For unittest, derive the module path for the exact target and invoke it directly, or otherwise constrain discovery so unrelated files cannot affect the verdict.

refutation.reason: The quoted line shows the unittest discover flag uses the directory path (start), not the target basename as a pattern to execute unrelated files. The discovery is rooted at the target's directory, which limits scope to that directory, not all matching files across the codebase.

probe.summary: Test-runner probe (`probes/closingB_probe_sandbox.py`, b9e2819976fe section; probe.py:196-207): a directory holding a PASSING test_target.py and a FAILING test_unrelated.py was probed on the target only: outcome='pass', runner summary 'Ran 1 test, OK' — the different-basename neighbour did NOT run. The same directory plus a FAILING subpkg/test_target.py (SAME basename, in a subpackage): outcome='fail', 'Ran 2 tests, FAILED' — the subpackage namesake DID run (discovery recurses and the module name still matches).
